## Briefing Note — UNESCO World Heritage Figures

**Sources:** `whc.unesco.org` — Criteria page (`/en/criteria/`), World Heritage List (`/en/list/`), List in Danger (`/en/danger-list/`), Statistics (`/en/list/stat/`).
**Access date: 5 September 2026.** All totals below are as displayed on that date.

---

### Table 1 — Figures safe to publish

| Figure | Value | Where verified |
|---|---|---|
| Properties on the World Heritage List | **1,273** | List page headline + statistics table |
| — Cultural | **991** | List page + regional table |
| — Natural | **240** | List page + regional table |
| — Mixed | **42** | List page + regional table |
| Transboundary / transnational properties | **51** | List page tile |
| Properties on the List in Danger | **58** | Danger List page ("The 58 properties…", Art. 11(4)) + List page tile |
| Delisted properties (not in the 1,273) | **3** | List page tile |
| States Parties with inscribed properties | **173** | List page + regional table |
| States Parties to the Convention | **196** (site dates this "as of October 2024") | List page text |
| States Parties with no inscribed property | **23** | Statistics page (and 196 − 173 = 23 ✓) |

### Table 2 — Regional breakdown (sums to the published total)

| Region | Cultural | Natural | Mixed | Total | % | States Parties |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Europe & North America | 501 | 74 | 13 | 588 | 46.19% | 50 |
| Asia & the Pacific | 228 | 73 | 13 | 314 | 24.67% | 36 |
| Latin America & Caribbean | 106 | 40 | 8 | 154 | 12.10% | 28 |
| Africa | 65 | 45 | 5 | 115 | 9.03% | 41 |
| Arab States | 91 | 8 | 3 | 102 | 8.01% | 18 |
| **Total** | **991** | **240** | **42** | **1,273** | 100% | **173** |

**Arithmetic checks I ran, all clean:** 991+240+42 = 1,273; the five regional totals sum to 1,273; each category column sums correctly; States Parties column sums to 173.

---

### The traps

1. **The criteria renumbering is not a simple shift.** Until end-2004 there were two separate sets (six cultural, four natural). The 2005 Operational Guidelines merged them into one set of ten. The old **natural** criteria map *non-sequentially*: N(i)→**(viii)**, N(ii)→**(ix)**, N(iii)→**(vii)**, N(iv)→**(x)**. Cultural (i)–(vi) are unchanged. Anyone assuming natural (i)→(vii) will be wrong on three of four. (Decision 06 EXTCOM 5.4, 2003.)

2. **Two symbols on the List page are shown with no readable definition — flagging this plainly.** The visible legend only explains the coloured diamonds (cultural/natural/mixed, and red for in-danger). The `*` and `#` markers appear against property names with no text key. I resolved both by cross-checking rather than guessing:
   - `*` = **transboundary / transnational**. Confirmed twice: the Danger List page *does* print this in its legend, and the List page exposes it only as a hover tooltip.
   - `#` = hover tooltip reads: *"As for 19 Natural and Mixed Properties inscribed for geological values before 1994, criteria numbering of this property has changed. See Decision 30.COM 8D.1."* Cross-checked against Los Glaciares National Park (Argentina, inscribed 1981, carries `#`), whose page now shows criteria **(vii)(viii)** — consistent with the mapping in trap 1.
   - Because these are hover-only, they are invisible in print, screen readers and copy-paste. Define them yourself if you reproduce the list.

3. **Why counting entries overshoots the total.** The 51 transboundary properties are listed under *each* participating State Party. Worked example: *Mosi-oa-Tunya / Victoria Falls* appears under both Zambia and Zimbabwe; *Mount Nimba* under both Côte d'Ivoire and Guinea. The "properties by State Party" table therefore sums to more than 1,273 by design. Never derive the total by addition.

4. **Some properties are counted in a region they are not in.** The statistics page carries an explicit warning that UNESCO's regions are administrative and "do not necessarily reflect the actual geographical location of countries," plus three named trans-regional cases each allocated to one region only: *Uvs Nuur Basin and Landscapes of Dauria* and the *Hyrcanian Forests* (both counted in Asia & the Pacific despite European extent), and *The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier* (counted in Europe & North America despite spanning Asia-Pacific and Latin America).

5. **Delisted properties still appear in the list, struck through** (e.g. Liverpool – Maritime Mercantile City, delisted 2021). The 3 delistings are *excluded* from 1,273 — don't re-add them.

6. **"Jerusalem (Site proposed by Jordan)"** is listed outside the normal State Party attribution. It is a reason the 173 figure should be quoted as published rather than reconstructed.

7. **Mixed dating.** 1,273 reflects the most recent Committee session, but the site tags the *ratification* count as "October 2024." Don't collapse these into one "as of" date — cite each as published, and re-check totals after the next session.

---

Two cautions on scope. I did not obtain a cultural/natural/mixed split *within* the 58 in-danger properties — that is not published as a headline figure and would need manual counting, so don't quote one. And figures in rows marked as session-dependent (1,273; 58; 51; 173) are precisely the ones that move, so the 5 September 2026 access date should travel with them in print.
